# Honeyicons

Honeyicons is a React icon library and a browsable SVG collection for chats, editors, and dashboards.

## Set up with a coding agent

Give your coding agent this prompt:

Set up @honeyicons/react using https://icons.0xhoney.com/setup.md

## React usage

import { Icon } from "@honeyicons/react";

<Icon icon="bell" size={24} />
<Icon icon="search" size={16} />
<Icon icon="moon" variant="bold" />

The icon prop takes a kebab-case icon name, typed as IconName, and variant accepts only the variants that icon has. Unknown names throw. Icon accepts standard SVG props, className, style, color, size, strokeWidth, variant, and an optional title for an accessible image label. Icons without a title, aria-label, or aria-labelledby are decorative. Give icon-only buttons an accessible name on the button.

Icon includes the full collection in the bundle. For fixed icons, use named imports such as import { Bell } from "@honeyicons/react" and <Bell /> so bundlers can remove unused icons.

## Conventions

- Render icons with Icon and names from the icon index. Do not invent names.
- Icons use a 24 by 24 viewBox, currentColor, and a default 1.8-unit stroke with rounded caps and joins.
- Use size={16} or size={24} for common interface sizes.
- Preserve supplied filled geometry. Some linear icons use filled outlines; strokeWidth does not change their baked-in weight.
- The variant prop accepts "linear" or "bold". Each icon defaults to its first variant: linear, or bold for bold-only icons such as most brand logos. Check an icon's variants before passing one; a variant the icon does not have throws.
- The collection is predominantly linear, with bold versions of brand logos and a few interface icons.
- The icon index at https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@honeyicons/react@latest/icons.json lists each icon's name, export, category, variants, and tags.

## Agent skill

Install the Honeyicons skill so coding agents look up real icon names before writing code:

npx skills add arjunkambj/honeyicons

## SVG

Browse /icons, search or filter the catalog, and select an icon to copy its code. SVG source files are maintained in the repository under icons/.

## Availability

React and standalone SVG are implemented in this repository. React Native and a consumer CLI are coming soon. There is no MCP server yet.
